Practised listing different pairs that make 10; next time, check this with a why or new-situation question.

end.parentNote: Asha practised making 10 using objects, counting, and everyday examples. Gauri found partners such as 7 and 3 and 6 and 4; the method of checking by counting was useful. Gauri still mixed up reversed pairs and sometimes treated 5 and 5 as the only pair, and this was not corrected at the last seen turn. At home, ask Gauri to find two ways to make 10 and say each pair in both orders, such as 3+7 and 7+3.
